body:
OBSERVED in source, 2026-08-23.

After a KEPUB package repair the app computes the audience of users who synced the affected
book and creates a per-user notice event (`cps/tasks/kepub_package_repair.py:107-131`). It is
delivered as a JSON inbox at `GET /api/v1/notices` (`cps/api/notices.py:23-38`).

Only the SPA consumes it: mounted globally in `frontend/src/components/AppShell.tsx:29-35`,
rendered with the re-sync guidance and a permanent dismissal in
`frontend/src/components/UserNotices.tsx:50-99`, and per-book at
`frontend/src/pages/BookDetail.tsx:305-312`. Searching the classic side for any consumer —
`notices`, `UserNotice` across `cps/templates/` and `cps/static/js/` — returns only unrelated
hits inside `js/libs/tinymce/license.txt`. There is no classic surface.

Why it matters for retirement: the plan keeps classic as the fallback during rollout, and this
is the direction the audit did not look. A user whose device holds a broken KEPUB, who falls
back to classic, is never told to re-sync — the one instruction that fixes their book.

A second, milder instance of the same blind spot: `/whats-new` is an SPA-only route
(`frontend/src/App.tsx:255-258`, `frontend/src/pages/WhatsNew.tsx:90-99`) with no classic page.
Not material on its own; recorded because two counterexamples make the pattern, not the
exception.

Action: either accept in writing that fallback users lose repair notices, or give classic a
minimal notice banner. Do not carry it as an unstated assumption.
title: Per-user notices are SPA-only, so a classic-fallback user never sees KEPUB repair instructions
